keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 561-594, a period Cliopatria draws inside its Kingdom of the Franks (about 0.68 M km2). 'In 561 Chlothar died, and his realm was divided between his four sons': Guntram received the old Burgundian kingdom, plus central France around Orléans (his chief city) and most of Provence (Francia page); when Guntram died in 592 'Burgundy went to Childebert in its entirety'. The old kingdom is Cliopatria's 523 shape; the radius around Orléans and the named region Provence are my reading of the page.

region.text: the old Burgundian kingdom, central France around Orléans and most of Provence

ledger.note: 561: Guntram receives Burgundy. 'In 561 Chlothar died, and his realm was divided between his four sons'; Guntram received the old Burgundian kingdom, central France around Orléans (his chief city) and most of Provence. The new state is the Frankish sub-kingdom, not the kingdom of Gundobad.

region.text: Toulouse, Agen and Nantes, with several other cities the page does not name

ledger.note: 595: Theuderic II inherits Guntram's kingdom. 'At his father's death in 595, he received Guntram's kingdom of Burgundy, with its capital at Orléans. He also received Toulouse, Agen, Nantes, and several other cities.' The other cities are not named.

region.text: the land between the Seine and the Loire, including the Breton frontier, that went to Theuderic after Dormelles

ledger.note: 600: Theuderic and Theudebert beat Chlothar II at Dormelles. They 'defeated Clotaire at Dormelles' and The territory between the Seine and Loire, including the Breton frontier, went to him after 600. The page gives no year for the cession; Cliopatria draws it from 602.

region.text: Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau and Champagne

ledger.note: 610: Theuderic II loses Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau and Champagne to his brother Theudebert II of Austrasia ('In 610, he lost Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau, and Champagne to his brother').

region.text: Austrasia, the realm of Theudebert II

ledger.note: About 611: Theuderic routs Theudebert at Toul. The page gives 'Toul (c. 611)'; the fighting is on the Burgundian-Austrasian frontier.
612: Theuderic defeats Theudebert at Tolbiac. He defeated Theudebert 'later at Tolbiac in 612', captured him and handed him to Brunhilda, who probably had him murdered.

region.text: Austrasia, the Rhineland, the Meuse and the Moselle

ledger.note: 612: Theuderic II takes Austrasia. 'In 612 Theuderic killed Theudebert, and the entire realm was again ruled by one man' (Francia page); the Theuderic page has him rule Austrasia from 612 to 613 and take both thrones.

region.text: Burgundy and Austrasia, united under Chlothar II

ledger.note: 613: Chlothar II takes the whole realm. Theuderic II died at Metz in late 613; Brunhilda placed Sigebert II on the throne of Austrasia, but Warnachar and Rado 'abandoned the cause of Brunhilda', Brunhilda and Sigebert were executed (613) and the realm went to Chlothar, who held Burgundy 613-629 and Austrasia 613-623; the Edict of Paris of 614 'reserved many rights to the Frankish nobles'. Cliopatria's Burgundian shape runs to 616 and is cut at 613.

region.text: Neustria and Burgundy, the realm of Clovis II

ledger.note: 639: Clovis II takes Neustria and Burgundy. He 'succeeded his father Dagobert I in 639' as king of the Franks in Neustria and Burgundy; Sigebert III kept Austrasia. Cliopatria draws the shape from 644; the page dates no division.

region.text: Neustria and Burgundy at Cliopatria's last year

ledger.note: 660: Cliopatria's last year for Burgundy. The pages opened give no end for Burgundy as a separate kingdom: Chlothar succeeded Clovis II (no year) and Childeric II was placed on the Austrasian throne; the Francia page has him assassinated in 675 after Ebroin removed Childebert in 661. The end is a bridging choice.

wars.name: Wars of Theuderic II and Theudebert II against Chlothar II

zones.text: the land between the Seine and the Loire

wars.outcome: Chlothar II and Fredegund took Paris and beat the two brothers at Laffaux (596); the brothers beat Chlothar at Dormelles (600) and took the land between the Seine and Loire; Chlothar invaded Theuderic's kingdom in 604 (Mayor Berthoald killed at Étampes).
wars.note: The page gives no 605 event; the 604 invasion is the last dated step.

wars.name: War between Theuderic II and Theudebert II
wars.outcome: Theuderic won Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau and Champagne in 610, routed Theudebert at Toul (c. 611) and defeated and captured him at Tolbiac (612), taking Austrasia.
wars.note: The 610 land is listed as lost by Theuderic in the page; the direction is the page's wording, 'he lost ... to his brother'.

wars.name: Chlothar II's conquest of Burgundy and Austrasia
wars.outcome: After Theuderic II's death the Burgundian and Austrasian nobles deserted Brunhilda and Sigebert II, who were executed; Chlothar II held all three kingdoms and issued the Edict of Paris in 614.

certainty.note: The pages name kings, cities and kingdoms (Burgundy, Austrasia, Neustria, Orléans, Toulouse, Champagne), never a surveyed line; the shapes are Cliopatria's outlines.

notes:
Split-off state: Cliopatria's 'Burgundian Kingdom' (414-660) is two states. The 413-534 kingdom of the Burgundians is burgundian-kingdom.json; this dossier takes the four shapes 602, 612, 644 and 656, which are the Merovingian partition kingdoms of Burgundy (Theuderic II's realm, then Neustria and Burgundy under Clovis II). They are listed in Cliopatria as members of the Kingdom of the Franks and Merovingian Empire umbrellas, which supports reading them as sub-kingdoms. The slug frankish-burgundy is new (slugify of 'Frankish Burgundy'); the colour agent must seed it. Validation prints 'no verdict' warnings for the 13 shapes 414-523: they belong to burgundian-kingdom.

Four pages were used (Francia, Theuderic II, Chlothar II, Clovis II), all opened for the sibling dossier. The Wikipedia field and the Wikidata id are null: no article describes this state; the row's id Q13590051 is the Burgundians'.

New keyframes: 561 (Guntram's Burgundy), 595 (Theuderic II's inheritance), 600 (the Seine-Loire land), 610 (the loss of Champagne and the Saintois) and 639 (Clovis II). They fill Cliopatria's gaps 561-601 and 639-643 and correct the end of 612-616 to 613. Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks shapes of 561-601 (0.68 M km2) and 617-643 contain the same land, so the kingdom-of-the-franks dossier (eu-07) should subtract Burgundy for those years, or the orchestrator should pick one drawing.

Not settled: (a) 614-638: Chlothar II (d. 629) and Dagobert I (d. 639) held Burgundy with its own mayor of the palace and the Edict of Paris of 614 recognised three kingdoms; the pages give no separate Burgundian territory and the Frankish row draws the land; this dossier lets the state lose all land in 613 and regain it in 639; (b) the end in 660 (confidence 1); (c) the extent of the Burgundian realm after 639 (the pages give 'Neustria and Burgundy' only; Aquitaine is not named on the Clovis II page); (d) Alsace and the Thurgau of the 610 loss were never inside the 602 shape; (e) the region names 'Champagne' and the 'Nancy' radius for the Saintois are my reading; (f) the capital after 639 is not given.

Gazetteer: all names used are in the gazetteer (Champagne, Alsace, Provence, Thurgau, the places Orléans, Toulouse, Agen, Nantes, Nancy).
